name: day-tank
title: Day Tank
description: A session budget rendered as a ship's day tank — the fill draws down as you spend, and while you compose a request a dashed ghost band previews exactly how much of it that request will take before you've sent anything.
useWhen: a live session/API budget where the question is 'how much do I have left, and can I afford what I'm about to send' — the fill is remaining STOCK, drawn down as spend happens, and its one unique move is rendering a pending request's estimated draw as a distinct pre-commitment ghost slice (dashed edge, breathing opacity) before the user has sent anything, which resolves into real drawdown with a single spring on send. Pick reed-vu instead for a live amplitude/RATE reading (tokens-per-second, a Web Audio spectrum) with no concept of a running total; pick tide-gauge-password instead for a liquid-level metaphor over input strength, not money.
instruction: Renders a session/API spend budget as a physical day tank: a slim vertical column (or a horizontal strip via `orientation="horizontal"` for compact toolbars), 6px radius, 1px --border, whose fill represents remaining budget and visibly draws DOWN as `spent` grows, never up — this is STOCK (what's left), not RATE, which is reed-vu's job. The fill is split, bottom-up, into two adjacent bands that always sum to exactly remaining/capacity: a 'safe' solid --foreground band at low (0.14) opacity for whatever of the remaining budget the in-flight request will NOT touch, and — directly above it, only while `pending` is greater than zero — a 'ghost' band at ~0.35 opacity sized to that pending estimate, breathing 0.25↔0.45 opacity on a 2.4s ease-in-out loop (stripped to a flat 0.35 under prefers-reduced-motion, per the reduced-motion contract below). The boundary at the very top of the fill (remaining/capacity) is a single 1px line that does double duty: with no pending estimate it's the plain meniscus, solid --foreground with 2px overshoot past both edges; the moment `pending` goes positive that exact same line cross-fades (300ms) to a plain 1px dashed --muted edge with no overshoot, marking the reading as provisional. `pending` is meant to be the live output of the consumer's own estimate(prompt, model, context) function, recomputed and passed down on every keystroke — the ghost band and its breathing update immediately as that number changes, with no debounce inside the component. A visually-hidden aria-live=polite region announces pending changes, but only material ones (>10% relative change from the last announced value) and only once per 3-second window, so a fast typist doesn't get a running commentary — a real spend change (a commit landing, a server correction, a refill) is announced in full and immediately, never throttled, since those are discrete, infrequent events. Sending is a single explicit signal: the parent flips `committing` true for the span between firing the request and the real result landing (keeping `pending` at its last live value throughout, per the contract), which triggers a one-shot, non-repeating transition — the dashed edge finishes cross-fading solid, and the ghost band's height eases to zero while the safe band grows to absorb it, both driven by the identical spring-eased transition (550ms, cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) — a single back-eased spring, not a bounce loop) so the tank's total silhouette never jumps mid-animation. An ordinary `spent` change with `committing` never having fired — a correction arriving on its own — eases in over a plain 400ms ease-out-expo; a `spent` DECREASE (a refill) eases in slower (900ms, same ease-out-expo curve, just unhurried) because a day tank filling back up is a different physical event than one draining. Under prefers-reduced-motion every one of those eases collapses to an instant snap and the breathing keyframe is dropped entirely — the dashed border alone (not motion) is what tells a ghost band apart from committed fill, so the component stays fully legible with zero animation. Beside the tank, in Geist Mono, sits the only text this component ever renders: the remaining amount large and bold, `/ capacity` small and muted below it, and — only while a live estimate exists — a third small line reading the pending draw ('− $0.41 next'); the accessible name for the whole thing lives in an aria-label (default 'Session budget'), never as visible prose. The tank itself is `role=meter` with `aria-valuemin=0`, `aria-valuemax=capacity`, `aria-valuenow=spent` (deliberately left unclamped if a caller lets spend exceed capacity — same honesty precedent as this registry's other budget gauges), and `aria-valuetext` spelling the exact sentence a sighted user reads off the gauge plus its readout ('$3.20 of $10 used, next request estimated $0.41'). It is NOT itself a keyboard control — there is nothing to focus or activate on the tank, by design; it's a passive display paired with whatever composer UI is driving `pending` and `committing`, which is why the demo wires it to a real textarea + send button rather than exposing any interaction on the tank. Pure DOM + CSS: every band and edge is a plain absolutely-positioned div colored via `bg-foreground`/`border-*` token classes and one literal `var(--muted)` dashed border — no canvas, no SVG, and nothing here is ever a numeric color literal, so both themes restyle for free.
